$comment: The parity contract for mocks/e-color-sort.html. Every promise the mock makes that a build could fail to keep, as a claim with the exact title of the browser/unit test that proves it. tests/mock-parity.test.ts requires a spec per claim once the claim's phase is declared COMPLETE in the plan's Status line, and guards the numbers here against the mock's own text. Add a claim when the mock gains a promise; never delete one to go green.

claims.claim: A bare /color-sort/ land shows the frame's poster (splash, title, pitch, setup card, Play) — not a board.
claims.spec: mock E1.1: a bare land opens the poster, not a board

claims.claim: The setup card's Mode defaults to Endless; Play starts level 1 (4 colours, 6 tubes) for a fresh record.
claims.spec: mock E1.2: Play from a fresh record starts endless level 1 with 6 tubes

claims.claim: With fewer than 5 solves, the Daily option is visible and disabled, and its row reads 'Unlocks after 5 solves · N to go' with the true N.
claims.spec: mock E1.3: Daily is visible, locked, and counts down to 5 solves

claims.claim: After the fifth solve the Daily option enables and a 'Today's puzzle · par N' chip appears on the poster; the Mode default stays Endless.
claims.spec: mock E1.4: the fifth solve unlocks Daily and the poster chip without moving the default

claims.claim: A shared ?r= daily result opens regardless of the gate (a deep link is a deep link).
claims.spec: mock E1.5: a shared daily record opens below the gate

claims.claim: With a game in progress the poster's primary is 'Continue · Level N' and resumes that deal.
claims.spec: mock E1.6: Continue resumes the in-progress level

claims.claim: Playing, band ③ carries exactly three stats — moves, level (or par), best — and the dock carries Undo · Hint · New game… · Restart · Settings.
claims.spec: mock E2.1: meters and verbs are the frame's, in the mock's order

claims.claim: The board's top edge is the same pixel before and after a pour, a deadlock, a hint and an undo (the frame's stability rule).
claims.spec: mock E2.2: the board does not move on pour, deadlock, hint or undo

claims.claim: At 390px every tube button is at least 44px wide and tall (drawn at 48).
claims.spec: mock E2.3: tubes clear the 44px tap floor at 390

claims.claim: No moves left is a toast overlaid on the stage with Undo and Restart, not an in-flow banner.
claims.spec: mock E2.4: deadlock is a stage toast, not a banner

claims.claim: A water pour is four Web Animations in sequence — lift 120ms, travel+tilt 200ms, pour 160ms per unit moved, return 200ms — at Normal speed.
claims.spec: mock E3.1: the water pour runs lift 120 / travel 200 / 160 per unit / return 200 at Normal

claims.claim: The source tube rotates about its lip (transform-origin at the mouth corner) and docks with the spout over the target's mouth.
claims.spec: mock E3.2: the source rotates about its lip and docks over the target mouth

claims.claim: The core applies the move at tap time; a tap during the return starts the next pour from the true state (no input lockout).
claims.spec: mock E3.3: a tap during the return is accepted against the true state

claims.claim: In the ball skin nothing tilts: each moved ball animates its own arc, 140ms per ball, landing in its slot.
claims.spec: mock E3.4: the ball skin hops balls one at a time, no tilt

claims.claim: In the bolt skin the nut unscrews (rotates as it rises off the thread), carries level, and screws down onto the target bolt, rotating the other way.
claims.spec: mock E3.5: the bolt skin unscrews, carries, and screws down

claims.claim: A partial pour (run of 3 into 1 free slot) animates exactly the units that moved.
claims.spec: mock E3.6: a partial pour animates only the units that moved

claims.claim: ?fast=1 collapses every pour animation to a frame so the existing rules specs keep their pacing.
claims.spec: mock E3.7: ?fast=1 collapses the pour to a frame

claims.claim: When a tube locks, the cap animates on and a completion cue fires once for that tube.
claims.spec: mock E4.1: a completed tube plays its cap and cue once

claims.claim: Undo animates the last pour in reverse rather than snapping.
claims.spec: mock E4.2: undo reverses the pour animation

claims.claim: Color Sort's settings section holds Look, Pour speed (Slow · Normal · Fast · Off), Fruit icons and Strict, after the common rows.
claims.spec: mock E5.1: the settings sheet carries Look, Pour speed, Fruit icons, Strict

claims.claim: Pour speed Off (or prefers-reduced-motion) runs no transform animation; the moved units cross-fade and a live region announces the pour with count and target.
claims.spec: mock E5.2: Off and reduced motion cross-fade and announce the pour

claims.claim: prefers-reduced-motion selects Off until the player picks a speed; the explicit pick wins thereafter.
claims.spec: mock E5.3: reduced motion is the default speed, not a lock

claims.claim: The sign-in offer appears under the result only after a solve, never on the poster or during play, for an anonymous record.
claims.spec: mock E6.1: the sign-in offer appears after a solve and nowhere else

claims.claim: The sign-in sheet is the atmo-provider sheet: open-signup providers with Create account and Sign in, invite-only providers behind Another provider with Sign in only, and a handle field.
claims.spec: mock E6.2: the sign-in sheet shows both panels and the create rule in both directions

claims.claim: Create account sends prompt=create in the PAR; Sign in sends no prompt.
claims.spec: mock E6.3: Create and Sign in are two intents in the PAR

claims.claim: Signing in binds the local record to the DID and sends no record anywhere; the header shows the person.
claims.spec: mock E6.4: sign-in binds the local record to the DID and publishes nothing

claims.claim: One local record per game, $type-shaped, holds stats (solved, strictSolved, streak, maxStreak, lastDay, bestLevel, played) and the in-progress game, behind a substrate seam.
claims.spec: mock E6.5: the record is one $type-shaped object behind a substrate

claims.claim: At ≥900px the rail shows the stats, the verb grid, This game (Mode, Level, Daily) and the settings rows inline.
claims.spec: mock E7.1: the desktop rail carries meters, verbs, This game and settings

claims.claim: Sound is synthesised in Web Audio, unlocked on the first gesture, silent when the frame's Sound row is off, with a distinct cue per skin.
claims.spec: mock E8.1: sound follows the Sound row and differs per skin

claims.claim: After each phase the shipped surface is re-captured with tools/mock-snaps.mjs and stands beside Proposed in the mock as Shipped, with the baseline sha bumped.
claims.spec: mock E9.1: the mock carries a Shipped capture from the current baseline
